title: Critical Power Incident Coordination
summary: Coordinate safe evidence review, cross-domain handoffs, escalation, and recovery validation.
objectives: Analyze a synthetic critical-power incident across power, service, network, and cooling signals.
Coordinate a documented handoff while identifying unsafe actions and uncertainty.

vocab.def: Evidence that modeled service and supporting systems returned to expected states.
Passing a concern to an authorized role when action is outside scope or risk is material.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: The incident is fictional. Do not operate panels, breakers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, transfer switches, or live PDUs.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Review A/B state, UPS alarm, load headroom, generator availability, rack impact, network state, cooling alarm, and recent maintenance. Identify the affected failure domain, likely dependencies, prohibited actions, and qualified teams for handoff.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Document known facts, uncertainty, safe next step, validation criteria, and recovery owner.

practice.prompt: What should an incident handoff include?
practice.answer: Timestamped observations, affected path/domain, uncertainty, safe next step, validation, and escalation owner.

quiz.question: What is the appropriate response to an uncertain energized-system condition?
options: Do not handle it; preserve evidence and escalate
quiz.answer: Do not handle it; preserve evidence and escalate

reflectionPrompt: Which condition required qualified professional escalation?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
